confirmed.title: The E1 noun/verb 'same ID and snapshot' parity check is tautological
confirmed.failure_scenario: getObject(P) and getWork(WORK) with scope {itemId:P} build the compared fields from the same work.world(context, worldScope) plus getInventory(worldScope) result. merged.putAll(world) overwrites workIds, obligations, contributions, ownerIds and evidenceRefs. The snapshot hashes only org|actor|asOf|knownAt|worldScope|world, not the operation or the requested id. The six equality assertions in e1-verb therefore compare one computation with itself. They cannot fail for any wrong world value (Finding 1's eligible 20 passes identically) or for wrong work-specific data. 'Same ID' is never checked either: nothing asserts $WORK is in E1_WORK_IDS or that the verb's data.ID equals $WORK. contributions is [] on both sides.
confirmed.evidence: ApplicationQueries.java:66-86: worldScope is built from scope keys only, world=work.world(...), merged.putAll(world), snapshot(context,snapshotScope,shared) with shared=world. e1-final.json:153-190 asserts only that verb fields equal the bound noun fields. The evidence shows identical snapshot 27e01d4b... and identical lists (obligations 15, contributions 0, ownerIds 1, evidenceRefs 11).
confirmed.fix: Assert the parity fields against independent oracles: SQL duty rows and owners for the QC/RETURN/SETTLEMENT duties, workIds == {WORK, SALES_WORK}, eligible 0. Assert verb identity (data.ID == $WORK). Compare across genuinely different entrypoints (REST vs MCP, per D20) rather than two operations backed by the same world builder.

verdict.reasoning:
I checked the claim against the reviewed commit 6fa7beb1 and it holds. ApplicationQueries.java:66-87 is the same at HEAD.

**How the code produces parity**
- For both getObject(P) and getWork(WORK) with scope {organizationId, itemId:P}, the shared path builds worldScope from scope keys only.
- It calls WorkReadHandler.world(context, worldScope). That method (WorkReadHandler.java:42-58) depends only on scope, not on the operation or the requested id.
- It merges in getInventory, then runs merged.putAll(world). This overwrites the handler's own work-specific obligations and contributions (getWork sets these for WORK alone at lines 28-29).
- snapshot() hashes org|actor|asOf|knownAt|worldScope|world.
- Result: the noun and verb answers are the same computation by construction.

**What the stored evidence shows** (de8d19ea actual-s4-native.json, actions e1-noun and e1-verb)
- Both have snapshot 27e01d4b...
- workIds are the same two IDs, ownerIds has 1 entry, obligations 15, evidenceRefs 11, contributions [].
- Both report eligibleQuantity 20 and heldQuantity 100.
- The verb's obligations list covers both works, not just WORK.

**What the E1 checks actually assert** (author.py:129-131)
- e1-verb only asserts that each verb field equals the value bound from the noun read.
- It does not assert data.ID == $WORK, that $WORK is in workIds, any expected duty kinds or owners, or eligible = 0.
- contributions is [] == [] because WorkContributions is only written by createWorkLink CONTRIBUTES_TO, which E1 never does. That comparison checks nothing.

**What could neutralize the finding, and why it doesn't**
- e1-final-independent's humanDuties operator (NativeS4TradeMain.java:112) checks for open human-owned duties of the QC, return and settlement kinds. But it reads raw DB rows (`mulino_work_read_obligationreferences`), not the API response.
- e1-current-warehouse checks eligible 0 only at placeId=W.
- So suppose WorkReadHandler.world returned obligations=[] and ownerIds=[] (or wrong ones) for every caller. Then e1-noun and e1-verb would still match, the raw-row check would still pass, and E1 would pass.
- That breaks the plan's E1 requirement that QC/return/settlement duties and owners be queryable (조회돼야 한다). It also breaks §13.3's rule to observe the API response, not only SQL.

**Why P2 and not higher**
- Making the two reads equal by construction is a legitimate way to meet §3.4's parity requirement. In this run the API did return the expected duty kinds and owner. So I found no product defect here; this is a weak, misleading test.
- The "same ID" part is minor.

confirmed.title: A second verified source naming a different receiving custodian is silently accepted when the confirm omits receivingCustodianId (custody conflict check is caller opt-in)
confirmed.failure_scenario: receipt60 is confirmed with receivingCustodianId=A, and both its event payload and original name A. A second source B for the same range (the D07 two-document case) names receivingCustodianId=B, another internal actor. matchSourceIdentity uses receiptPayloadMatches, which ignores the custodian, so it returns MATCHED, and the link adds a second VERIFIED chain to the same canonical. confirmReceipt for source B without the slot then has custodian==null: requireEvidencedCustodian is skipped and so is the duplicate branch's custody comparison. The result is APPLIED with duplicate=true. The canonical now carries verified chains naming {A,B}, while the segment keeps custodian A. That segment remains fulfillable, because FulfillmentCommands.requireWarehouse only checks for some internal custodian. No HELD outcome, conflict record or duty is produced. Supplying the slot with the same evidence would instead return HELD EVIDENCE_CONFLICT, so detection depends on what the caller sends. ReturnCommands has the same pattern.
confirmed.evidence: ReceiptCommands.java:55: `if(custodian!=null){requireEvidencedCustodian(...)}`. Line 57: the duplicate branch compares custody only `if(custodian!=null&&...)`, then returns applied(...,true). EvidenceReconciliation.java:162 receiptPayloadMatches checks range, item, lot, place, work, quantity, unit and time, but not receivingCustodianId. FulfillmentCommands.java:44 requireWarehouse only checks internalCustodian(segment.custodianId). ReceiptGatewayPostgresTest only covers a single chain whose event and original disagree, not two chains.
confirmed.fix: On every confirm, including slot-less and duplicate confirms, collect custodian statements from all verified chains of the canonical. If they disagree with each other, or with the segment's recorded custodian, return HELD EVIDENCE_CONFLICT and open a reconciliation duty (and block fulfillment of the segment). Add a backend test with two sources naming different custodians.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The scenario is reachable at the reviewed commit; ReceiptCommands.java is identical at 6fa7beb1 and at HEAD.

1. **First confirm records A.** receipt60 is confirmed with slot A. requireEvidencedCustodian (ReceiptCommands.java:72-84) sees only chain A, so named={A}. ReceiptStockPrimitives.java:22 then writes custodianId=A on the new segment.

2. **Source B links to the same canonical.** Source B is recorded as a second provisional observation for the same rangeRootId, with receivingCustodianId=B in both the original blob and the event payload. This mirrors the existing test actual60plus40CrossSourceDuplicate..., with a custodian added. EvidenceReconciliation.match still returns MATCHED:
   - receiptPayloadMatches (line 162-163) checks range, start, item, lot, place, work, quantity, unit and time, but never receivingCustodianId.
   - Lines 117-123 only flag a different physical scope, a different effectiveFrom or a different time precision.
   
   link() then finds the single canonical for that scope/time (lines 183-184) and adds a second VERIFIED chain through verifyReviewedReceiptCanonical. The only link-time impact hook is AssessmentCorrectionImpact.evidenceLinked (lines 34-44). It invalidates assessments and handles delivery corrections, but never re-checks receipt custody. A grep confirms receivingCustodianId is read only in ReceiptCommands, ReturnCommands and ReceiptStockPrimitives.

3. **A slot-less confirm of B is accepted as a duplicate.** custodian is null, so requireEvidencedCustodian is skipped (line 55). The duplicate branch's custody comparison is guarded by `custodian!=null` (line 57). same() compares only start, quantity, item, lot, unit, place and purchaseLine, and the canonical matches. The result is APPLIED with duplicate=true, and the segment keeps custodianId=A.

4. **Fulfillment still proceeds.** FulfillmentCommands.java:44 requireWarehouse only checks internalCustodian(segment.custodianId), so reservation and dispatch of that segment continue.

5. **Detection depends on the slot.** If the slot is supplied on that same confirm (A or B), the verified chains name {A,B} and the confirm returns HELD EVIDENCE_CONFLICT. Even then no duty or conflict record is produced, so the conflict is surfaced only when the caller sends the slot. The conflict also persists after linking even if no second confirm is ever sent.

**Mitigating points, which keep this at P2:**
- The s4e contract text (docs/execution/s3-receipt/contracts.md:56-63) scopes the duplicate-source custody conflict to the slot case ("중복 출처가 slot으로 다른 보관 주체를 주장하면"). The behaviour therefore literally follows the implementation's own contract.
- The same contract's general rule ("검증 출처끼리 다른 보관 주체를 지명하면 HELD EVIDENCE_CONFLICT") and the plan's principles still point to this being a gap. Those principles are §4.3 (conflicting sources are reconciled, not last-write-wins) and §4.1/§4.2 (custody is known only from evidence). In practice, the first confirm decides custody and later contradicting verified evidence is ignored.
- Linking B requires a human reviewer's MATCHED reconciliation, so this is not a forgery path.
- No quantity is double counted and there is no authorization bypass.
- The plan does not explicitly mandate re-checking receipt custody evidence, so P1 is not justified.

**ReturnCommands part of the claim (weaker):** its duplicate branch requires the same eventId and the same canonical (ReturnCommands.java:35), so a different-source observation cannot take the duplicate path. Only the "late-linked conflicting chain is never re-evaluated" aspect carries over there.

Overall the defect stands as P2: an order-dependent custody-conflict check that existing tests do not cover. ReceiptGatewayPostgresTest tests disagreement within a single chain only, never two chains naming different custodians.

confirmed.title: E1 noun/verb entry-point parity is tautological; API surfacing of the three human duties is never asserted
confirmed.failure_scenario: A product whose getObject/getWork answers carry `obligations: []`, `ownerIds` without the duty owners, or no sales-work ID still passes E1: `e1-noun` (line 131) binds E1_SNAPSHOT/E1_DUTIES/E1_OWNERS/E1_WORK_IDS from the product response and `e1-verb` (line 153) only asserts that getWork returns the same values. Both queries are 'world' operations: ApplicationQueries.queryInternal merges `work.world(context, worldScope)` with worldScope={organizationId,itemId} into both responses (backend/src/main/java/com/mulino/application/core/ApplicationQueries.java:66-82) and derives `snapshotRevision` as SHA-256 of that same world (lines 83-87), so equality of snapshot/obligations/owners/workIds holds by construction for any content, including empty. No assertion anywhere in the E1 flow checks that the public query answer contains OPEN QUALITY_REVIEW / RETURN_* / SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duties with human owners (plan §13.3 '각각의 미해결 의무와 owner가 조회돼야 한다'); only the independent SQL `humanDuties` operator over mulino_work_read_obligationreferences (line 49) checks the read table.
confirmed.evidence: author.py:130-131 generates e1-noun with `bind` only and e1-verb with `expected: $E1_*`; NativeS4TradeMain.execute('query') line 77-78 binds from `result.response()`; ApplicationQueries.java:70 `Map<String,Object> world=work.world(context,worldScope);` and :80 `merged.putAll(world)`, :83 `snapshot(context,snapshotScope,shared)` with shared=world. The flow-wide scan of `expected` values bound from product responses lists exactly these six e1-verb assertions.
confirmed.fix: In e1-noun add assertions on `/data/obligations` (matchingRows for kind in {QUALITY_REVIEW, RETURN_QC_REVIEW, RETURN_COMMERCIAL_REVIEW, RETURN_SETTLEMENT_REVIEW, SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE} with status OPEN, ownerid equal to a fixture human alias) and that `/data/workIds` contains both $WORK and $SALES_WORK; cross-check E1_DUTIES against rows bound from the SQL observe (bindRows) rather than from the previous product response; keep e1-verb but add the same content assertions so parity is checked on non-vacuous data.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. It holds at 6fa7beb1; the cited e1 files and ApplicationQueries are unchanged at HEAD.

**What the E1 flow checks**
- In `verification/actual/s4/e1-final.json`, `e1-noun` (author.py:130) only binds E1_SNAPSHOT, WORK_IDS, DUTIES, CONTRIBUTIONS, OWNERS and EVIDENCE from the product's getObject response. It has no assertions.
- `e1-verb` (author.py:131) only asserts that getWork returns those same bound values.
- `NativeS4TradeMain.java:76-78` confirms that a query action binds from `result.response()` and that `equals` compares against the bound value.
- No other S4 native action checks API-level obligations. I listed every getObject, getWork and getObligations action across the e1, c4 and e2 scripts. The only other ones are revision-binding reads with no assertions.

**Why the parity holds by construction**
- `ApplicationQueries.java:67-84`: both getObject and getWork are world operations. Each response's data is the handler data overwritten with `work.world(context, worldScope)`, and `snapshotRevision` is the SHA-256 of scope plus that same world.
- `WorkReadHandler.world` (lines 42-58) builds workIds, ownerIds, obligations, contributions and evidenceRefs only from the item-scoped world.
- So equality holds whatever the content, including empty lists. The one exception is a scope difference (for example, getWork adding the work's lotId), so "tautological" is slightly overstated. The check still guards the routing invariant against regressions, but it says nothing about content.

**Why the SQL checks don't neutralize it**
- The only duty check in E1 is the `humanDuties` operator (`NativeS4TradeMain.java:112`). It runs over SQL rawRows of `mulino_work_read_obligationreferences`, not the API answer.
- The backend tests are no different. ReturnGatewayPostgresTest and SettlementCommandPostgresTest assert RETURN_* and SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duties with `jdbc.queryForObject` on the same read table. S1ReadIntegrationTest checks ownerIds generically, not these duty kinds.
- A system whose world() or authorization filter dropped the sales work or its obligations would still pass E1. For example, the reader's grant could fail to cover $SALES_WORK, so the RETURN_* duties never reach the API answer.

**Plan and record**
- Plan §13.3 requires that each unresolved QC, return and settlement duty and its owner can be queried. Plan line 456 says not to rely on SQL alone and to observe API responses together with duties.
- `docs/execution/step-3-s4.md:72-74` says the human duties are cross-checked against the same-ID/snapshot noun/verb queries and the independent ledger. That cross-check does not exist, so the record is misleading.
- An earlier review found the same weakness in the oracle case (cases-b-10, P2, `docs/execution/claude-rereview-steps-1-2.md:106`), and it has come back in the native suite.

**Why P2, not P0**
- The product currently behaves correctly. The actual run evidence (`docs/execution/evidence/step3-s4/de8d19ea/actual-s4-native.json.gz`, e1-noun and e1-verb) shows API obligations containing OPEN QUALITY_REVIEW, RETURN_QC_REVIEW, RETURN_COMMERCIAL_REVIEW, RETURN_SETTLEMENT_REVIEW and SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE with a non-empty owner, and both workIds.
- So no wrong outcome happens today. The defect is a weak acceptance assertion plus a misleading record.

confirmed.title: The humanDuties oracle matches by kind only; C1's 'existing responsibility retained' passes on an unrelated purchase-Work QUALITY_REVIEW, and the suspended sales reservation has no duty
confirmed.failure_scenario: In C1, revokeDispositionBasis suspends the 20 BOX allocation on SALES work 8205c11a. The only new open duty is QUALITY_REVIEW with quantity 40 on the PURCHASE work 5c63a4ba, recorded on the basis's work at QualityCommands.java:52. No duty with owner, nextAction and nextCheck exists for the suspended reservation on the sales Work or line. Plan §4.2 requires reduced availability to become '부족 의무와 대체 배분 대상', and C1 requires '기존 예약 책임은 남고'. The humanDuties operator counts any OPEN, valid, human-owned row of the kind, with no binding to Work, subject or quantity and no uniqueness check. It therefore passes here, and would also pass with duplicated duties (the same weakness applies to E1's five kinds).
confirmed.evidence: c1-sale-revocation.json:618 asserts humanDuties ['QUALITY_REVIEW']. In the evidence, c1-final-independent obligationreferences has QUALITY_REVIEW OPEN, quantity 40, workid 5c63a4ba (PURCHASE); the allocation b01a80d1 is SUSPENDED, quantity 20, workid 8205c11a (SALES); there is no duty on 8205c11a. NativeS4TradeMain.java:112 only requires count>0 per kind.
confirmed.fix: Extend humanDuties with expected workId/subject/quantity and an exact count. In the product, open a reservation-shortage duty on the allocation's Work whenever an allocation is suspended by a hold or revocation.

verdict.reasoning:
Overstated. All that holds up is a minor weakness in the native oracle.

1. The duty is not unrelated. At 6fa7beb1, QualityCommands.java:52 records QUALITY_REVIEW for revokeDispositionBasis on the revoked basis's own workId, with the basis's range and quantity. In the de8d19ea native evidence, the only QUALITY_REVIEW in C1 is 96ba2d46. Its scopejson.domainSourceId is b844ebf0, which is exactly the dispositionBasisId returned by c1-revoke-sell40, and that response also lists suspendedAllocationIds [b01a80d1]. The duty sits on work 5c63a4ba because the commercial basis was recorded under that Work. The oracle therefore matched the duty the revocation itself created. If the product failed to create it, C1 would fail, because no other QUALITY_REVIEW exists in that organization.

2. The humanDuties assertion is not what proves that the existing reservation responsibility remains. C1 checks that separately in c1-final-independent: matchingRows requires allocation $ALLOCATION to be SUSPENDED with quantity 20 and to be the only allocation, and dispatches/sales execution effects must be 0. c1-after-revoke-responsibility then checks getInventory reservationResponsibilityQuantity=20 and eligible/unreserved=0. That covers plan §13.2 C1 ("기존 예약 책임은 남고 신규 예약·출고는0").

3. The product gap is not a clear plan violation. The §5.3 row for placeHold/releaseHold/recordDispositionBasis/revokeDispositionBasis requires "영향 예약 정지·의무 보존", and the product does both: it suspends the affected allocation and opens a duty with an owner and next check. §4.2's "부족 의무와 대체 배분 대상" is written for 정정/QC reductions. The SUSPENDED allocation stays a replacement target, since FulfillmentCommands accepts SUSPENDED for replaceAllocation. The sales Work 8205c11a stays ACTIVE with its owner and an unmet goal, which matches the philosophy's "출고 중지·대체 할당·S1 책임 유지". The validity sweeper's per-allocation INVENTORY_VALIDITY duty comes from a different plan rule (§line 323) that only applies to sweeps. Revoke and sweep do treat suspension inconsistently, but no plan text requires a separate duty on the sales Work after an explicit revocation.

4. Duplicate duties are already caught in the backend. FulfillmentPostgresTest c1 and QualityPostgresTest:69 both assert COUNT(*)=1 QUALITY_REVIEW for the owner after revoke.

What is left: NativeS4TradeMain.java:112 humanDuties only requires count>0 per kind. It does not tie the duty to its Work, domainSourceId or quantity, and it does not check uniqueness. So a native run would accept a wrongly bound or duplicated duty in C1/E1/E2. That is a real but small weakness in the test, not a demonstrated product defect, so P3.

unverifiedP3.title: The native suite never observes the custody effect; the 'no inference from the confirming actor' claim rests on manual inspection
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: No observe in any S4 flow asserts mulino_inventory_quantitysegments.custodianid or ownerid. If confirmReceipt inferred custody from the confirming actor (reader, who is internal) instead of the evidenced supervisor, E1/E2/C1/C4 would still pass, because reserveQuantity only requires some internal custodian. s4e-custody/README.md:37-41 verifies the supervisor custody by reading raw rows by hand.
unverifiedP3.evidence: grep finds no 'custodianid' pointer in any verification/actual/s4/*.json. author.py name_receiving_custody only injects slots. The e1 final raw rows show custodianid d423a88a (supervisor) on W segments, but this is not asserted.
unverifiedP3.fix: Add SQL assertions: receipt-derived W segments have custodianid=$supervisor and ownerid null; the return segment and the customer-site segment have custodianid null.

unverifiedP3.title: The bank-effect-0 oracle is vacuous (constant response field plus the wrong table)

The independent check counts mulino_trade_settlement_paymentreferences, which hold payment-reference observations; plan §6 says 지급 참조≠은행 이체. It never inspects mulino_runtime_outbox, which the snapshot captures (one dispatchPurchaseOrder row). A change that enqueued a bank or payment outbox operation from matchInvoice would still pass E1.
unverifiedP3.evidence: SettlementCommands.java:42 `result.put("bankEffect","0")` and effects.put("bankEffect","0"). e1-final.json asserts only paymentreferences size 0. The evidence shows mulino_runtime_outbox with 1 row (dispatchPurchaseOrder PENDING).

unverifiedP3.title: Negative native commands accept any rejection reason; the waiver-reuse case cannot distinguish single-use approval enforcement; the assertion count is inflated
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: c4-waive-deficit2-without-decision and c4-waive-deficit2-reuse accept any REJECTED outcome; both observed a generic FORBIDDEN 'Unavailable scope'. The reuse case targets an assignment that is already WAIVED, so any product rejects it whether or not single-use approval is enforced. e2-repeat-recovery-denied and e2-repeat-disposal-denied accept any CONFLICT. unverifiedP3.evidence: In the evidence: c4-waive-deficit2-reuse is REJECTED with FORBIDDEN 'Unavailable scope' and no assertions; e2 repeat cases are CONFLICT with RECALL_EVENT_ALREADY_APPLIED, not asserted. unverifiedP3.title: Duplicate-source receipt confirm without the custody slot neither validates nor surfaces conflicting custody evidence, and an omitted slot on the first confirm makes custody permanently unrecordable
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: Scenario A: receipt60 verified evidence names custodian S and is confirmed with the slot (segment.custodianId=S). A second verified source for the same range names custodian R and is confirmed without `receivingCustodianId`: line 55 skips requireEvidencedCustodian (custodian==null) and line 57 skips the custody comparison, so the duplicate is APPLIED with no EVIDENCE_CONFLICT and no duty although verified sources disagree on custody. Scenario B: first confirm omits the slot (custodianId=null, 'unknown'); a later duplicate source carries the evidenced slot S: `!custodian.equals(old.custodianId)` is true (S vs null) and the command is HELD 'Duplicate source names different receiving custody' — the correctly evidenced custody can never be attached to the already-created segment, which then stays unreservable (FulfillmentCommands requires a confirmed internal custodian).
unverifiedP3.evidence: ReceiptCommands.java:55 `if(custodian!=null){requireEvidencedCustodian(...)}`; :57 `if(custodian!=null&&!custodian.equals(inventory.object(c,"QuantitySegments",old.get("segmentId")...).get("custodianId")))throw new DomainError("HELD","EVIDENCE_CONFLICT",...)`. Native E1's sourceB60 original omits receivingCustodianId (author.py:36 CUSTODY_RECEIPTS={'receipt60','receipt40'}) so neither scenario is exercised; ReceiptGatewayPostgresTest custody tests (lines 162-178) cover single-source cases only.
unverifiedP3.fix: In the duplicate path, always run the evidence custody check of the new chain (named set of the new source) against the existing segment custodian: disagreement -> HELD EVIDENCE_CONFLICT (or an open duty), agreement -> idempotent duplicate; allow a later evidenced slot to set custody on a segment whose custodianId is null via an explicit, audited custody-record step rather than treating null as 'different'. Add a native/backend case for both scenarios.

unverifiedP3.title: acceptance-contract.json expectations are never reconciled with native results
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: The contract declares E1 expectations (unresolvedHumanDuties QC/RETURN/SETTLEMENT, entrypointParity 'same ID and snapshot', bankEffects 0) but no runner reads it: grep over verification/ and verify finds no consumer. The combined evidence summary reports the native suite PASS without any machine link from contract cases to the assertions that cover them, so a flow edit that drops an assertion (e.g. humanDuties) would leave the contract untouched and still 'PASS'.
unverifiedP3.evidence: `grep -rn acceptance-contract verification verify` returns nothing; NativeS4TradeMain.run only records flowHash/fixtureHash and `fullCaseCoverageClaimed=false`.
unverifiedP3.fix: Have NativeS4TradeMain (or the coverage verifier, plan §13.4) load acceptance-contract.json and emit per-case PASS/NOT_RUN by mapping each contract key to named assertion IDs, failing the receipt when a required case has no executed assertion.

unverifiedP3.title: linkCanonicalOccurrence re-runs match() and persists a second Reconciliations row per link
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: Every successful link (receipt, delivery, return, invoice originals in E1) calls match() for the recheck, and match() unconditionally inserts a new Reconciliations row (line 140). Each verified fact therefore carries two reconciliation records with identical claim/decision but different IDs and recordedAt; getReconciliation lists both and reconciliation counts/audit history are inflated by the product itself, which can mask a genuine second human review.
unverifiedP3.evidence: EvidenceReconciliation.java:173-175 `var checked=match(c,new Review(...),"linkCanonicalOccurrence")`; :140 `r.insert("Reconciliations",row)` inside match with no 'dry-run' flag.
unverifiedP3.fix: Split match() into a pure evaluation used by link() and the persisting command path, or mark the recheck row with a distinct role (e.g. decision source 'LINK_RECHECK') so history distinguishes human review from the automatic fence recheck.
